extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators (PD/PIs), applicant organizations, and Authorized Organization Representatives (AORs) seeking to appeal an NIH initial peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing and submitting a written appeal of the NIH initial peer review of a grant application, including required content, allowable bases for appeal, timing, required organizational concurrence, submission and withdrawal procedures, and possible outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an appeal (four acceptance criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal is a written communication from a PD/PI and/or applicant institution that meets the following four criteria: 1) is received after issuance of the summary statement and up to 30 calendar days after the second level of peer review, 2) describes a flaw or perceived flaw in the review process for a particular application, 3) is based on one or more of four allowable issues, and 4) displays concurrence from the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All four elements must be met for a submission to be considered an appeal rather than a grievance. If any element is missing (e.g., no AOR concurrence), the submission will not be treated as an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal must be received after issuance of the summary statement and up to 30 calendar days after the second level of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs may establish specific deadlines for appeals to be available at Council meetings; in no circumstance will an appeal be accepted before the summary statement has been transmitted to the PD/PI or later than 30 calendar days after the relevant Council meeting. If the appeal is received by the IC deadline for Council availability, the PD/PI and AOR will receive a written explanation no later than 30 calendar days after the Council meeting. If received after the IC deadline, the PO will provide a written explanation within 30 calendar days of receipt about the IC's plan for making the appeal available to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) concurrence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal letter must display concurrence from the AOR of the applicant organization for the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although content may originate from PD/PI or other organizational officials, the AOR must either send the letter directly to the Program Official (PO) or send concurrence to the PD/PI who will forward materials and AOR concurrence to the PO. A communication from the PD/PI or other official only, or with a 'cc' to the AOR, will not be accepted. The same AOR-concurrence requirement applies to requests to withdraw an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of the appeal letter
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal letter will be accepted only if the letter: 1) describes the flaws in the review process for the application in question, 2) explains the reasons for the appeal, and 3) is based on one or more of the allowable process-related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters that do not describe process flaws, do not explain reasons, or are not based on allowable issues will not be considered appeals and will be treated as grievances under IC-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable bases/issues for an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals must be based on one or more of the following process issues: evidence of bias by one or more peer reviewers; conflict of interest as specified in regulation at 42 CFR 52h.5; lack of appropriate expertise within the Scientific Review Group (SRG); factual error(s) made by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the outcome of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals based solely on differences of scientific opinion will not be accepted. The description of factual errors should indicate how the error could have altered the review outcome substantially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on contacting reviewers or Council members
rubrics_metrics.description: At no time should the PD/PI or an official of the applicant organization attempt to contact individual members of the Scientific Review Group (SRG) or individual members of the Council to discuss the review of an application or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting reviewers or Council members could jeopardize confidentiality of the review process and is explicitly forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-appeal consultation with Program Official (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants concerned about procedural aspects should consider the summary statement and contact the appropriate NIH Program Official (PO) to ask questions about the summary statement and review outcome and to obtain advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO can recommend resubmission strategies under NIH policies (e.g., NOT-OD-10-080), reconsideration of project intent, or submitting a new application with substantial differences. Contacting the PO is encouraged before filing an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of appeal receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: The PO will send the PD/PI and/or institutional official, and AOR, an acknowledgement letter within 10 days of receipt of the appeal letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural promise of acknowledgement; keep records of submission dates and acknowledgment for timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of non-qualifying submissions as grievances
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter that does not meet the appeal criteria and/or does not include the concurrence of the AOR will not be considered an appeal letter, but rather a grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievances will be handled according to IC-specific procedures. Appeals involving potential conflict of interest or ethical violations by NIH staff will be referred to the appropriate Deputy Ethics Counselor before further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of the appeal by NIH staff
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH review staff and program staff will consider the basis of the appeal letter and evaluate its merit; if both support the appeal, the original application, without additional materials or modifications, will be re-reviewed by the same or a different SRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only if both review and program staff support the appeal will re-review occur. Re-review uses the original application only — no new materials or modifications are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible Council outcomes and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Only two outcomes are possible following Council consideration of an appeal: 1) Council may concur with the appeal and recommend that the application be re-reviewed; 2) Council may concur with the SRG's recommendation and deny the appeal. A Council recommendation concerning resolution of an appeal is final and will not be reconsidered by NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if factual errors are evident, Council may determine they were unlikely to alter the final SRG outcome and deny the appeal. No action by Council is equivalent to concurrence with the SRG and denial of the appeal. The PD/PI and applicant organization must not contact Council members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if re-review is recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: If Council recommends re-review, the original application will be re-reviewed without additional materials or modifications and may be re-assigned to a subsequent review round or a different SRG, which typically delays the final funding decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outcome of the re-review is final and cannot be appealed again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If review staff and program staff do not support the appeal, or do not agree on its merit, the PD/PI and/or an institutional official may elect to withdraw the appeal letter; the withdrawal request must display concurrence from the AOR and be submitted to the PO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedural mechanics for withdrawal mirror submission: content may originate from PD/PI or other officials but the AOR must send the withdrawal or concurrence directly to the PO or to the PD/PI to be forwarded. Communications only from PD/PI or other official (with AOR cc) will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of appeals involving NIH staff conflicts or ethics issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals involving potential conflicts of interest or violations of ethical conduct rules on the part of an NIH staff member or other federal employee will be referred to the appropriate Deputy Ethics Counselor for consideration and resolution before any further review or action on the appeal is taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such referrals occur prior to further appeal processing and may require separate investigative or ethics procedures.
